question: Which proposed-edit, accept/reject and attribution policies belong to Suggestions, and which should reuse native authored changes?
trigger: The owner asked for a best-api-review audit of every open ledger unit, frozen from status at fe0e9599a6 on 2026-10-04 (39 units), and judged afresh because earlier verdicts came from a weaker model. It asked for verdicts only, so no plan, build or panel follows in this run. This scope was open as pursue-unbound at queue position 16. It is not the unit next returned, which was reads.
requirements: Suggestions, accepted edits and comment actions attribute to the authenticated application user; authentication stays app policy.
Native authored requires a non-empty author at the first write and allows actorless reads (2026-09-16 authored writer-identity Stop).
Existing suggestions load through the complete initialValue, preserving authors and change IDs; initialization never replays edits under switched identities (docs/vision/plate.md).

Native authored owns suggestion schema, mutation, review scan and decisions; Plate owns mode controls, decorations, copied review UI and product defaults; Comments keeps an independent thread lifecycle.
Editing + Markup replacement resolves only a fully contained change-and-dependency set in one undoable transaction; incomplete selections stay protected (2026-09-23).
Mounted-view intent and projection stay on EditorRoot authored; no plugin-global mode.
evidenceReuse: Reused the 2026-09-13 to 2026-09-23 suggestions records, the decision page, the 2026-09-22 plan and its execution record as evidence. Rechecked on the live tree that projected-selection-target.ts and mutation-controller.ts carry the closed-set accept-then-replace bridge, and that suggestion.spec.ts holds the multi-block removal and protected-dependency browser cases. Inspected BaseSuggestionPlugin, SuggestionPlugin, PlateAuthoredPlugin, the Editor runtime type, BaseCommentsPlugin current-user writes, the public suggestion doc, and every registry example that seeds suggestions or sets userId or currentUserId. mutation-controller.ts has an uncommitted 3-line typed-text wrap from another session, unrelated to the bridge. withPlite.ts is uncommitted and was not cited.
summary: The job is to attribute proposals, accepted edits and review replies to the acting application user, and to load multi-author suggestions without replaying commands. Native authored ownership, EditorRoot authored, the Plate suggestion feature and the 2026-09-23 closed-set direct replacement are all in live source with browser tests. The remaining gap is attribution. Plate fixes the native authorId resolver to Reflect.get(editor.runtime.userId), Comments keeps its own currentUserId, public docs tell apps to set both, and copied import UI copies both by hand. SuggestionPlugin and AIChatPlugin hard-depend on that fixed DefaultAuthoredPlugin, so apps cannot pass native authored options. The only Plate way to act as another author is mutating runtime.userId, which the playground does on every mount while replaying proposals. The strongest deletion, removing Plate's userId bridge and having apps install authored({ authorId }) directly, removes the reflection but keeps two identity inputs and needs a descriptor-composition answer for SuggestionPlugin and AI. So the direction is one typed editor-session actor that authored attribution and Comments both read, plus canonical createAuthoredReviewDocument hydration for the playground (discussion-demo already uses it).

callSites.current: createEditor({ plugins: [...SuggestionKit, ...DiscussionKit, CommentsPlugin.configure({ initialState: { currentUserId: user.id, users } })], userId: user.id }); DefaultAuthoredPlugin resolves Reflect.get(editor.runtime, 'userId'); acting as another author means editor.runtime.userId = 'bob' (playground replays proposals this way before hydrating).
callSites.proposed: Proposed: createEditor({ plugins: [...SuggestionKit, ...DiscussionKit, CommentsPlugin.configure({ initialState: { users } })], userId: user.id }); authored attribution and Comments read one typed session actor (no currentUserId, no Reflect bridge, no runtime mutation); multi-author fixtures load as initialValue: createAuthoredReviewDocument({ accepted, revisions: [{ id, authorId, createdAt, change }] }).

reconciliation.reason: Its closed-set direct replacement rule is adopted in source and browser tests and stays settled; this review moves the scope's open work to attribution, not to that rule.

reconciliation.reason: Its completion claim matches live source (projected-selection-target.ts resolve/blocked split, accept-then-replace in mutation-controller.ts); proof stays historical, not re-run.

reconciliation.question: Should rich-text-editor initialize suggestions through plugin configuration like comments, instead of replaying authored edits?
reconciliation.reason: Its target to delete fixture replay and runtime author switching is not adopted in playground-demo.tsx, which still replays proposals per mount under mutated runtime.userId with history skipped.

alternatives: Keeping the current design (Stop) is rejected. One person is two independently writable identities that public docs teach and import UI copies, attribution rests on a reflective untyped runtime bag, and the flagship demo breaks the initialization law.

Deleting createEditor userId and DefaultAuthoredPlugin, so apps install authored({ authorId, retainHistory }) and SuggestionPlugin and AI compose from it, is the strongest deletion. It removes the Reflect bridge and unlocks native options, but it leaves Comments' separate currentUserId and needs a descriptor-composition design, because SuggestionPlugin and AIChatPlugin depend on one exact descriptor. The plan should compare it.

One typed editor-session actor in Plate (createEditor userId), read by the default authored resolver and by Comments, with Comments currentUserId and the Reflect reads deleted, is the selected direction. Apps pass one input, no hidden contract remains, and independent features share the session fact.
Having Comments derive the current user from authored is rejected, because it couples optional suggestions into comments-only installs.
Moving actor identity into Plite core is rejected. The native authored resolver is already the neutral API, and session identity is Plate product state.
Reopening native authored ownership or restoring a Plate suggestion engine is rejected. All earlier targets landed, and no new evidence contradicts them.
proofLimits: Source review only; no test, typecheck or browser command was run. The duplicate-truth failure (userId and currentUserId diverging, stale own-author colors in suggestion.tsx after a runtime switch) is inferred from source, not reproduced. Whether mid-session actor switching is a real product job or demo-only is unresolved and belongs to the plan. List, table, second-author concurrency, IME and mobile suggestion parity remain the audited backlog from 2026-09-13 and are not judged here. mutation-controller.ts and withPlite.ts carry uncommitted work from other sessions; neither decisive claim rests on those diffs.
